 This Mfa Is Filed U/S.173(1) Of Mv Act, Against The
 Judgment And Award Dt.07.09.2019 Passed In Mvc
 No.1531/2017 On The File Of The Additional Senior Civil

Judge And Additional Mact, Hassan, Partly Allowing The
Claim Petition For Compensation And Seeking Enhancement
Of Compensation.
 This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day, The
Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

With consent of learned counsel appearing for both the parties, matter is taken up for final disposal,
even though it is listed for Admission.
Heard learned counsel appearing for the appellant and learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2- Insurance Company.
2. This appeal arises out of the judgment and award in MVC No.1531/2017 passed by the learned Additional Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Hassan dated 07.09.2019.

3. The appellant-petitioner contended that on 22.06.2016 at about 2.00 p.m., when he was riding his bike to go to his shop, the driver of the offending lorry insured by respondent No.2 herein, drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against petitioner's bike.
As a result, the petitioner has sustained severe injuries.

He was NC: 2023:KHC:21082 shifted to Janapriya Hospital, Hassan, wherein he took treatment and spent huge amount for treatment and he having suffered permanent disability is entitled for compensation.
It is contended that the petitioner was aged 27 years at the time of the accident and working as a Mechanic.
4. On issuance of notice, respondents No.1 and 2 appeared before the Tribunal, but respondent No.2 alone contested the petition by filing objection.
5. Respondent No.2- Insurance Company denied the age, income and avocation claimed by the petitioner and contended that the petitioner had not suffered any permanent disability in the accident.

It has contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive,
exorbitant and untenable in law and there is violation of the policy by the driver of the insured vehicle.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed necessary issues and the petitioner was Saifulla Shariff @ Saifulla vs Karigowda on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190892634/
2 examined as PW-1 and the doctor who treated him was examined as PW-2 and 14 documents were marked as Exs.P1 to P14.

Respondent NC: 2023:KHC:21082 No.2 has not led any evidence, but a copy of Aadhar card of the appellant is marked as Ex.R1.
7.

The Tribunal, after hearing both the sides, awarded the compensation under different heads as below;
 Towards pain and sufferings - Rs.60,000.00  Towards Medical expenses - Rs. 1,56,926.00  Towards diet, food, - Rs. 10,000.00  nourishment, attendant and  conveyance charges  Towards loss of future - Rs.1,73,400.00  earning capacity  Loss of income during laid - Rs.17,000.00  up period  Towards loss of amenities - Rs. 15,000.00  Towards Future Medical - Rs. 20,000.00  expenses  Total - Rs.4,52,326.00 8.
Being aggrieved by the said judgment and award, the petitioner is before this Court in appeal.
9. On issuance of notice, respondent No.2 has appeared before this Court and notice to respondent No.1 was dispensed with at the risk of the appellant.

Learned counsel for the appellant contended that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side and it has not considered the avocation of the petitioner and the disability suffered by him.
It is contended that nature of the injuries clearly show that there was disability and the notional income considered by the Tribunal is also not proper and correct.
Therefore, learned counsel for the appellant has assailed the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

11. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2-Insurance Company has contended that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and there is no need for reconsideration of the amount awarded by the Tribunal.
12. It is contended that the petitioner- appellant had suffered fracture on the lower limb, chest injury, facial injury and mild head injuries.
The Tribunal has considered the discharge summary and other documents regarding the injuries suffered by the petitioner.

The petitioner contends that he was a Mechanic, aged 27 years as per the Aadhar Card and he has NC: 2023:KHC:21082 suffered permanent disability of 30% of the lower limb and as such, he is entitled for a higher compensation.

Saifulla Shariff @ Saifulla vs Karigowda on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190892634/
3 13.
On a careful examination of the available records, it is evident that the petitioner is aged about 27 years and therefore, the appropriate multiplier would be '17'.
PW.2 had opined that there is disability of 30% to the right lower limb and the petitioner being a mechanic, there cannot be any dispute that the permanent disability would be 1/3rd of the limb.
Hence, the disability of 10% held by the Tribunal is proper and correct.
The Tribunal has assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.8,500/-.

It is relevant to note that the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for settlement of the disputes before the Lok-Adalat prescribed notional income of Rs.9,500/- in respect of the accident pertaining to the year 2016.

In umpteen number of cases,
this Court has held that the guidelines issued by the KSLSA are in general conformity with the wages fixed under the Minimum Wages Act.
Therefore, the notional income of the petitioner is considered at Rs.9,500/- per month.
In view of the above discussion, the compensation under the head of 'loss of future earning capacity' is calculated as Rs.9,500/- X 12 X 17 X 10% = Rs.1,93,800/-.

As a consequence, the compensation under the head of 'loss of income during laid up period' also needs to be enhanced and considering the nature of the injuries suffered by the petitioner, it can be safely be said that he was unable to resume his work at least for a period of three months.
Therefore, 'loss of income during laid up period' is calculated as Rs.9,500/- X 3 = Rs.28,500/-.
15. The compensation awarded by the Tribunal under the head of 'pain and suffering' being Rs.60,000/- is just, proper and correct and it needs no enhancement.

16. Similarly, the compensation under the head of 'medical expenses' to the tune of Rs.1,56,926/-
and the compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards 'future medical expenses' also do not require any enhancement.

17. The petitioner was inpatient for a period of 16 days and therefore, it would be just and proper to award a sum of NC: 2023:KHC:21082 Rs.20,000/- under the head of 'conveyance, attendant charges, nourishment etc'.
18.
The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.15,000/- under the head of 'loss of amenities in life.
In the considered opinion of this Court, 'loss of amenities' needs to be enhanced and the same is awarded at Rs.20,000/-.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.4,99,226/- under the following heads:
 SL. AMOUNT  PARTICULARS  NO. (IN RS.)
 1 Towards pain and sufferings 60,000/-
 2 Towards medical expenses 1,56,926/-

Towards conveyance,
 3 attendant charges, 20,000/-
 nourishment etc  Towards loss of future earning
Saifulla
Shariff
@ Saifulla vs Karigowda on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190892634/

4  4 1,93,800/-
 capacity  Loss of income during laid up  5 28,500/-
 period  6 Towards loss of amenities 20,000/-
 Towards future medical  7 20,000/-
 expenses  TOTAL 4,99,226/-
 Less awarded by Tribunal 4,52,326/-
 Enhancement 46,900/-
 NC: 2023:KHC:21082  19.
Thus, the petitioner is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.46,900/- with interest and therefore, the appeal deserves to be allowed in part.

Hence, the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified by awarding a sum of Rs.46,900/- in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal together with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
(iii) The respondent No.2 Insurance company is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount within a period of six weeks from the date of this order.
(iv) A sum of Rs.20,000/- awarded under the head of 'future medical expenses' will not carry any interest.
(v) Rest of the order of the Tribunal stands unaltered.
Sd/-
